pr_title: Add TLS close_notify handler to http server
pr_body:
> "close_notify" alert is used to indicate orderly closure of one
> direction of the connection.  Upon receiving such an alert, the TLS
> implementation SHOULD indicate end-of-data to the application.

This PR addresses issue when HTTP client sends TLS close_notify alert and wait for response from our HTTP server. 
But we dont handle close_notify alerts today, only full connection termination. Some clients might hang for a while until other timeouts fire up.

In this change I introduce an event listener for SslCloseCompletionEvent in the Netty4HttpPipeliningHandler, that handles close_notify alerts. When we receive alert we will close connection immediately. It might introduce server response truncation, but we rely on client to send close_notify when no more data is expected from the server.

Added warning logging, can be spotted now in unit and integ tests
```
[2024-06-25T21:08:49,310][WARN ][o.e.h.n.Netty4HttpPipeliningHandler] [node_t1] received TLS close_notify, closing connection [id: 0xfb96648b, L:/[0:0:0:0:0:0:0:1]:13484 - R:/[0:0:0:0:0:0:0:1]:63937]
```

Fixes #76642
pr_comments:

Thanks @Tim-Brooks for the feedback! I fixed leaking buffers.

issue_context.title: `close_notify` not sent when incoming connection is half-closed and quiescent when using TLS1.3
issue_context.body:
**Elasticsearch version** (`bin/elasticsearch --version`): confirmed in 7.14.0, likely others

**JVM version** (`java -version`): Bundled

**OS version** (`uname -a` if on a Unix-like system): confirmed on Mac, likely others

**Description of the problem including expected versus actual behavior**:

When closing an incoming connection that was using TLS1.3 the remote end sends a `close_notify` alert and may then wait for Elasticsearch to indicate there's no more data to receive with its own `close_notify` before starting to tear down the underlying TCP connection. However Elasticsearch does not send a `close_notify` even if it's finished responding to every request on the channel, so the client may wait forever.

This only seems to happen with TLS1.3 due to a change in the spec vs earlier versions, see https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc8446#section-6.1:

>   Each party MUST send a "close_notify" alert before closing its write
>   side of the connection, unless it has already sent some error alert.
>   This does not have any effect on its read side of the connection.
>   Note that this is a change from versions of TLS prior to TLS 1.3 in
>   which implementations were required to react to a "close_notify" by
>   discarding pending writes and sending an immediate "close_notify"
>   alert of their own.  That previous requirement could cause truncation
>   in the read side.  Both parties need not wait to receive a
>   "close_notify" alert before closing their read side of the
>   connection, though doing so would introduce the possibility of
>   truncation.

In particular with TLS1.2 and earlier we react with an immediate `close_notify` even if there's still data to send on the channel.

I expect this happens with transport connections too, but I've only confirmed it for HTTPS ones.

**Steps to reproduce**:

1. Connect to the HTTPS port and complete a TLS1.3 handshake.
2. Optionally perform some HTTP requests and receive the responses.
3. Close the TLS context with a `close_notify` message.
4. Observe that no `close_notify` message is returned.

**Provide logs (if relevant)**:

Here's a packet capture of an example session: [tls1.3.pcapng.gz](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/files/7006162/tls1.3.pcapng.gz)

At t=0s we open the connection; at t=1s we do the TLS handshake; at t=2s we do a HTTP request and get a response, at t=3s we send the `close_notify` but get no response until at t=4s we just drop the connection.
comments: It is _possible_ but it's not great, the whole point of this change in TLS1.3 is to avoid the possible truncation that might happen in TLS1.2 if the `close_notify` is sent while there's still responses pending. Bringing back that behaviour isn't the right solution IMO.

FTR the obstacle to fixing this is writing a test which exposes the bug, which needs quite low-level control over a TLS-enabled HTTP client in order to get it into a state where the TLS session is closed but the underlying TCP channel remains open. It should be possible to do something similar to `org.elasticsearch.http.netty4.Netty4HttpClient` by adding in the relevant TLS handlers into its pipeline.

review_comments: I have not investigated the test failure much. But I'm pretty sure these are going to need to be released at the end of the test.
Or else the leak detector will fire.

Tests make sense, but I think we'll also need some integ tests showing how this interacts with the rest of the system, particularly the task cancellation mechanism (which it doesn't today, but it'll need to).

I'm still thinking should we cancel or not. If we serve all requests while channel is writable then we dont need additional handling for cancelation. If channel is not writable, client decided not to wait, it will go through exception path, which exists today.

Although it is certainly possible to keep serving responses as you propose, it's also legitimate to cancel tasks and send the resulting exception responses, or indeed to just tear down the connection without sending any of the remaining responses, so this is more of a design question than a technical absolute.

I couldn't find any clients which might send a `close_notify` while awaiting responses - AFAICT this only happens on the abort path or when dropping an idle connection from a pool.

You are right, looking further into HTTP and TLS RFC's closing connection on `close_notify` make sense. Serving all responses and closing connection should be handled with `Connection: close` header in HTTP1. 

In TLS prior to v1.3 `close_notify` should discard all pending writes and close connection. TLS v1.3 tries to address [truncation attack](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transport_Layer_Security#:~:text=142%5D%5B143%5D-,Truncation%20attack,-%5Bedit%5D) by letting application layer to figure out how to close connection, we probably want to handle logout requests (oidc, saml) fully without truncation. I think in scope of this PR closing connection should be a good step forward.

I don't think truncation attacks are a possibility here, we always send either a `Content-length` header or else a properly-terminated chunked-encoded message so clients can tell if a response is incomplete at the HTTP layer. But this isn't the right place to discuss this more deeply - if you think there's a security issue in this area then please [mail security@elastic.co](https://www.elastic.co/community/security) with details.

Changed code to close connection immediately in all cases. Found that `SslHandler` triggers `userEvent` on `close_notify` `SslCloseCompletionEvent`, so I updated `Netty4HttpPipeliningHandler` to listen this event and close connection.

Also added integ test - SecurityNetty4TransportCloseNotifyIT. It's pretty similar to unit test, but on internalCluster. Have to use custom http client to send close_notify, I tried to hijack apache's http client sslEngine, but it got pretty messy.

>  I think we'll also need some integ tests showing how this interacts with the rest of the system, particularly the task cancellation mechanism (which it doesn't today, but it'll need to).

Since there is no cancellation now, is there something I should do with current tests?

> Since there is no cancellation now,

I think task cancellation should be hooked-up by default with this implementation. Since you close the channel, that will propagate through the listener framework and cancel tasks (I think).

`Netty4HttpChannel#addCloseListener`.
Nice! Is it worth to test cancellation in integ test? If yes, what rest operation would be a good example?

> Nice! Is it worth to test cancellation in integ test?

I will take another look at this PR later today. 

But IMO, if "HTTP Close triggers Task cancellation" triggers task cancellation is already tested, then this PR only needs to validate the "SSL client close_notify" leads to channel close.

However, I don't know if that test exists. My initial perusal of the code is that we do not have this test at an HTTP level (which we should). I would say this PR should implement it if it is missing.

I would look in `RestActionCancellationIT` and other classes in that qa package (`SearchRestCancellationIT`,  `ClusterHealthRestCancellationIT`, etc).

It looks like these are testing task cancellation through the http layer. I would do a bit of investigation and look at how the "cancellation" is implemented. I _think_ it might be through closing the http connection. But that appears to be a bit deep in the apache code and we should confirm it.

If those tests are sufficient then I think we are covered at the moment.

I added action cancellation test.

`RestActionCancellationIT` and `SearchRestCancellationIT` call request.abort() which indeed close connection. 
With help of neat plugin `CancellableActionTestPlugin` I found it's pretty easy to add integ test here for action cancellation - `testSendCloseNotifyCancelAction`
